title: Depth expansion and lateral compression vary inversely, conserving fish volume

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Depth expansion and lateral compression vary inversely, conserving fish volume

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In related fishes, expansion in one transverse dimension tends to be compensated by compression in the other, so that volume at a given length changes less than linear dimensions; the plaice is about twice as deep and half as thick as the haddock and has almost the same length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: plaice vs haddock: depth \times 2, thickness \times \tfrac{1}{2}, k = W/L^3 nearly equal

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVII: On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the very fact that the two dimensions tend to vary _inversely_ already assures us that, in the general process of deformation, the _volume_ is less affected than are the _linear dimensions_.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVII, “On the Theory of Transformations, or the Comparison of Related Forms”; topic “Three-dimensional transformations of fishes”. Scope: related fish species differing in body depth and width (e.g. haddock and plaice, shark and skate)

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: plaice vs haddock: depth \times 2, thickness \times \tfrac{1}{2}, k = W/L^3 nearly equal

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch17-18: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The directional covariance, example ratios and length-weight coefficient give clear tests. Combining broad trait data with open scans provides enough coverage for a strong comparative analysis using standard methods.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure length, depth, width and mass across related fishes, test negative depth-width covariation and compare variation in W/L^3 with each linear dimension; separately test the haddock-plaice ratios.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
FishBase length-weight records are not always paired with 3D shape.

Preservation and posture alter body width.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.82
data existence: 0.88
operationalizability: 0.94

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: FishBase already holds the length-weight half of the claim for thousands of species, including the named pair, and a k comparison is immediate. The inverse relation between depth and thickness needs body width, which the same database covers only patchily. The volume-conservation statement is testable now for many species, and the full geometric tradeoff is testable only where both transverse dimensions were published.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across related fishes, test whether body depth and body width vary inversely and whether the length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3 changes less than either linear ratio, including the specific claim that plaice is about twice as deep and half as thick as haddock at similar k. An inverse depth-width relation with stable k would support the claim; independent depth and width, or a large k difference for that pair, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Body width is recorded far less often than length-weight parameters, so the inverse-compensation half is data-limited.

Length type and seasonal condition shift k independently of the depth-width tradeoff.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.66
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data existence: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.52

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Among related teleost species (same family), relative body depth (depth/length) and relative body width (width/length) vary inversely, so that the length-weight coefficient k = W/L^3, a proxy for volume at a given length, varies less across species than either relative transverse dimension.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py downloads the Dryad version zip, verifies the specimen CSV against Dryad's SHA-256 digest, keeps the 16,377 specimens with positive mass, SL, depth and width, and takes geometric species means (6,091 species). For the 5,670 species in the 195 families with >= 5 species it computes d = ln(depth/SL), w = ln(width/SL) and k = ln(mass/SL^3), centres each on its family mean, and computes the Spearman correlation of centred d and w and the SDs of centred d, w and k. Per-family correlations and SDs are written to derived/families.csv; the plaice/haddock ratios are reported separately.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Species means from FishShapes v1 specimens (standard length SL, maximum body depth BD, maximum fish width FW, mass M; specimens with all four > 0). Variables per species: d = ln(BD/SL), w = ln(FW/SL), k = ln(M/SL^3). Families with >= 5 species are kept and each variable is centred on its family mean. (A) Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05. (B) the SD of family-centred k is smaller than the SDs of family-centred d and of family-centred w. SUPPORTS if A and B both hold.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. REFUTES if the Spearman rho between family-centred d and w is >= 0 AND the SD of family-centred k is >= the smaller of the SDs of family-centred d and w. Any other outcome is MIXED. Fewer than 20 qualifying families or 200 species: inconclusive (underpowered).

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: Spearman rho between family-centred ln(body depth/SL) and ln(body width/SL) across teleost species

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's 'expansion in one transverse dimension compensated by compression in the other' is read as negative covariation of depth and width at a given length among related fishes; 'related' is operationalized as the same family (FishBase family names used in FishShapes). Length is standard length; 'thickness' is maximum fish width; 'volume at a given length' is mass/SL^3 (Thompson's k uses weight, so mass is the direct quantity). Family-centring removes between-family differences so that the comparison is among related species, as Thompson's haddock/plaice and shark/skate examples are. Because ln k is approximately d + w + ln(density x shape factor), condition B can hold only if d and w covary negatively; it is the 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions' clause. Secondary, reported but not part of the verdict: Thompson's named pair, plaice (Pleuronectes platessa) vs haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus), if both are in the data: depth ratio expected ~2, width ratio ~0.5, k ratio ~1. Note they are in different orders, so this pair is not 'related' by the family criterion.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: FishShapes v1: functionally relevant measurements of teleost shape and size on three dimensions (Price et al. 2022)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Within families, relatively deep species are also relatively wide, not narrower: the family-centred correlation is +0.53, positive in 90% of the 195 families (median +0.56). As a result ln k varies more (SD 0.35) than ln depth/SL (0.22) or ln width/SL (0.18), the opposite of Thompson's 'volume less affected than the linear dimensions'.

Both ratios are divided by standard length, so overall elongation (slender vs stocky species) makes them covary positively. The pre-registered test follows Thompson's own framing ('at a given length'), but it does not isolate depth-width compensation at fixed cross-sectional area; an analysis that removes elongation (e.g. using depth/width directly or a cross-section measure) was not pre-registered and was not run.

Thompson's named pair is partly borne out: plaice is 2.09 times as deep relative to length as haddock (expected ~2) and 0.64 times as wide (expected ~0.5, inside the pre-registered 0.35-0.7 band), but its k is 1.44 times haddock's, outside the pre-registered 0.8-1.25 'nearly equal' band. This pair is descriptive only and not part of the verdict.

Specimens are preserved museum fish; mass and width can change with fixation and ethanol storage, and specimens were chosen as adult-sized, not at matched length. These add noise to k but are unlikely to reverse the sign of a +0.53 correlation across 5,670 species.

Species means rest on 1-3 specimens; intraspecific variation and measurement error inflate all three SDs, and k (three measurements combined) gets the most.

preregistered_at is the time of the pre-registration commit (78fafafa); the committed pre-registration carried an estimated time (21:40Z) written before committing. The data were first downloaded after that commit; criteria are unchanged.
